# Secret ballot (`secret_ballot`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: helped by alphabet_writing, printing_press
- Core idea: Each voter marks his choice unseen and drops it in a sealed box, so nobody can know how he voted. A bribe or a threat is then wasted, because the buyer or landlord cannot check that he got what he paid for. The working design: one uniform official ballot listing all candidates, a screened booth, a list of voters ticked off once, a sealed box, and a count in public watched by all sides. For the illiterate, use tokens, balls or symbols.
- Pitfalls:
  - Ballots printed by the parties in different colours or sizes are not secret: observers see which one goes in
  - Keeping the vote secret but also the count: the count must be public, or the counters decide
  - No voter list means stuffed boxes and repeat voters
  - Applying it to representatives: voters need secrecy, legislators' votes should be public so they can be held to account
  - Expecting easy agreement: many serious thinkers, J. S. Mill among them, held that open voting was a public duty
- History: greece: 5th–4th c. BC – Athenian jurors vote with pebbles and later bronze ballots with hollow or solid hubs, held so that the choice is hidden; ostracism by inscribed potsherds; india: c. 4th–3rd c. BC – the Buddhist monastic code (Vinaya, Cullavagga IV) describes voting with wooden tickets (salaka) by secret, whispered or open method; rome: 139 BC – lex Gabinia introduces written ballots for elections, extended to trials and legislation 137–107 BC; Cicero complains that it weakened the nobility's control; europe: 1268 – Venice elects the doge with balls (ballotte, the origin of the word ballot); 1795 French constitution requires secret voting; 1872 British Ballot Act; global: 1856 – the Australian colonies of Tasmania, Victoria and South Australia enact the government-printed ballot and polling booth (Tasmania's act is dated February, Victoria's March); adopted by most democracies by 1900; americas: 1888 – Massachusetts and Louisville adopt the Australian ballot
- Read:
  - Malcolm Crook & Tom Crook, Reforming Voting Practices in a Global Age: The Making and Remaking of the Modern Secret Ballot in Britain, France and the United States, c.1600–c.1950, Past & Present 212 (2011)
  - Mogens Herman Hansen, The Athenian Democracy in the Age of Demosthenes (1991)
